newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen easing on absence of incentives.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen easing on absence of incentives.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen easing on Wednesday on the absence of buying incentives which would keep investors on the sidelines, traders said.
The SET Index fell 6.78 points to close at 556.67 on Tuesday in thin 2.5 billion baht trade. The SET 50 ended at 40.35.
"Right now it is difficult to persuade clients to go into the market. I think they are waiting for key banks to fall further before buying," said a trader at a Bangkok Bank affiliated brokerage firm.
Finance One is expected to fall further at the start of its ex-rights period.
"We don't think the time is right to buy Finance One until the stock stands above two or three baht for a week or so," said the trader.

Reports that industry minister Korn Dabaransi is prepared to help troubled Alphatec Electronics Plc will likely generate local interest though some traders said his comments were too vague to encourage much institutional buying activity.
The market is also anxious to see new government measures for boosting the finance sector.
